claims.implementation: WorkflowGraphDocument (Package 1) is the sole canonical authority - no resolve_authority refusal exists, unlike C-24's CodeGraph, because MS §Visual Workflow Studio names it the authority directly. WorkflowGraphStore (Package 2) persists it as immutable, semver-versioned revisions: revision_number and semver are always derived from stored rows, never accepted from a caller, and document_of recomputes the content hash from stored declared content on every read, refusing a stored/recomputed mismatch as RevisionIntegrityViolation rather than trusting the stored column.
claims.evidence: arch: backend/tests/structural/test_workflow_authority.py (14 tests, Package 5) proves execution.workflow constructs no second graph model, no second revision store and no second execution-plan cache anywhere in the context. integ: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_graph_store.py (12 tests, Package 2) proves publish/latest/history/document_of against a real SQLite file across process reopens (the Reopener pattern), including the immutable-revision and hash-mismatch refusals.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (arch, integ) are supplied.

claims.implementation: CompiledExecutionPlan.derive (execution_plan.py, Package 3) deterministically builds a dispatch-ready view from a WorkflowGraphDocument's already-normalised nodes()/edges() (frozenset-backed, sorted rendering - see graph_model.py's determinism-by-normalisation), hash-bound to that document's content_hash. require_fresh refuses (StaleDerivedRepresentation) the instant the bound hash no longer matches the store's current revision hash for that workflow. The executor (Package 5) calls plan.require_fresh(record.bound_revision_hash) before every single dispatch, not once at start - _run()'s loop and every _plan_for() call.
claims.evidence: unit: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_execution_plan.py (9 tests, Package 3) proves derive is a pure, deterministic property (rebuilding from identical content yields an identical plan) and require_fresh's refusal in isolation. integ: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_executor.py's real multi-step runs (Package 5) exercise require_fresh being checked on every real dispatch against a real published revision, not merely as a standalone property.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (unit, integ) are supplied.

claims.implementation: The same require_fresh mechanism as ARK-REQ-0064, evidenced from the non-execution angle: a CompiledExecutionPlan whose bound_revision_hash disagrees with the store's current hash for that workflow raises StaleDerivedRepresentation before any node dispatches - the plan is refused, not silently re-derived or executed against stale content. The executor's _plan_for() re-derives and re-checks the plan on every resume (start/resume_after_signal/approve), so a revision published mid-execution cannot cause a later step to run against the old graph.
claims.evidence: prop: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_execution_plan.py::TestRequireFresh proves the refusal for an arbitrary stale hash, not one hand-picked example. integ: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_executor.py's WAIT/HUMAN APPROVAL pause-and-resume tests (Package 5) prove a real paused execution re-validates freshness on every resume against the real store.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (prop, integ) are supplied. Distinct from 0064 in subject (refusal of stale execution, not derivation correctness) though the same mechanism backs both, matching the register's own two-row split.

claims.implementation: WorkflowExecutor (executor.py, Package 5) composes - never duplicates - every prior authority: the canonical WorkflowExecution machine (Phase 3) is the sole transition authority (every lifecycle_state write comes from machine.evaluate().target), WorkflowGraphStore is the sole revision authority, CompiledExecutionPlan.require_fresh is checked before every step. The executor holds no second copy of graph content, no second transition table and no second revision-freshness rule.
claims.evidence: integ: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_executor.py + test_workflow_executor_pause_and_recovery.py (41 tests) drive real multi-step executions entirely through the composed authorities against a real SQLite file. arch: backend/tests/structural/test_workflow_authority.py (14 tests) proves structurally that execution.workflow declares no duplicate canonical authority, no shadow lifecycle table and no shadow state-machine literal - the same discipline test_the_registry_declares_no_state_of_its_own uses for Project.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (integ, arch) are supplied.

claims.implementation: construct_dispatch.py's evaluate_construct (Package 5) evaluates real, deterministic per-construct decisions from declared facts (node.parameters, the document's own edges, and a persisted counter for LOOP/RETRY/WAIT) for all 10 canonical control constructs. Every non-logic node dispatches as one real execution.durable job (submit -> begin_attempt -> complete_attempt via the pre-declared execution.workflow -> execution.durable sibling edge), for all 9 non-logic kinds. Every dispatch - leaf or logic - is recorded as one WorkflowNodeExecutionRecord row, carrying the revision_hash bound at that exact step.
claims.evidence: integ: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_executor.py + test_workflow_executor_pause_and_recovery.py (41 tests, Package 5) produce real evidence rows for all 10 kinds and all 10 constructs against real persistence and real durable jobs. backend/tests/structural/test_workflow_ui_coverage.py (Package 8) additionally proves, in one comprehensive real execution, that the exact set of kinds/constructs the Studio UI offers all appear in real evidence - with a negative control proving the comparison is not vacuous.
claims.note: The single register evidence key (integ) is supplied, doubly - once per-construct/per-kind in Package 5, once as a comprehensive cross-check in Package 8.

claims.implementation: control.policy's WorkflowApprovalGate (Package 4) is the sole answer to whether a HUMAN APPROVAL decision counts: assert_may_record refuses any actor in the canonical stable_mutation.prohibited_actors set (already names workflow, MS Constitution 6), and is_enforced_approval additionally refuses a non-APPROVED decision or one bound to a stale graph revision. The executor's approve() (Package 5) calls both before ever transitioning WAITING_APPROVAL -> RUNNING or enqueuing the approved node's outgoing edges - HUMAN APPROVAL is an evaluated policy stop the executor cannot bypass, not a visual element.
claims.evidence: sec: backend/tests/security/test_workflow_approval_gate.py (12 tests, Package 4) proves the prohibited-actor and stale-revision refusals in isolation. integ: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_executor_pause_and_recovery.py's HUMAN APPROVAL tests (Package 5) and backend/tests/surfaces/test_command_workflow_api.py::test_the_workflow_actor_is_refused_403 (Package 6) prove the enforcement through the real executor and the real HTTP surface. frontend/tests/e2e/workflow-studio.spec.ts's fifth test (Package 7) proves it a third time through a real browser: the workflow actor's approval attempt is refused with ARK-ERR-0133 and the execution remains WAITING_APPROVAL, then a real human-reviewer approval completes it.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (sec, integ) are supplied, reinforced by a real e2e negative path beyond what either key strictly requires.

claims.implementation: A structural cross-check (backend/tests/structural/test_workflow_ui_coverage.py, Package 8) rather than a new acceptance.engine production module - execution.workflow, surfaces.command AND acceptance.engine are all at max_public_surface_per_context's 40-of-40 ceiling, so the check is the comparison itself, run every time this suite runs, exactly as test_contract_drift.py already proves the transport contract with no dedicated production module of its own. It publishes one real C-20 graph exercising every one of the 10 canonical node kinds and 10 canonical control constructs, drives it through a real WorkflowExecutor across both real pause points, and asserts every kind/construct frontend/src/features/workflow/vocabulary.ts declares (the Studio's actual palette) appears in the resulting real evidence.
claims.evidence: integ: backend/tests/structural/test_workflow_ui_coverage.py::test_every_ui_declared_kind_and_construct_ran_for_real drives the real comprehensive execution and asserts full coverage. test_a_ui_node_type_without_evidence_is_detected is the negative control (test_contract_drift.py's anti-vacuity idiom): with one kind's evidence rows removed, the same comparison reports exactly that kind missing, proving the check is not vacuous.
claims.note: The single register evidence key (integ) is supplied, plus an anti-vacuity negative control the register does not itself require but this repository's convention throughout every comparable control (test_contract_drift.py, test_dependency_rules.py, etc.) always includes.

claims.implementation: The same ADR-0004 mechanism cited for 0064/0065 (CompiledExecutionPlan.derive/require_fresh, Package 3), evidenced here specifically through the real executor's per-step invalidation checks (Package 5): every resume path (start, resume_after_signal, approve) re-derives the plan from the store's current revision and calls require_fresh before advancing the frontier, so a stale derived representation is structurally incapable of reaching a dispatch.
claims.evidence: prop: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_execution_plan.py (Package 3) proves require_fresh as an exhaustive property over stale/fresh hash pairs. integ: backend/tests/execution/test_workflow_executor.py's real published-revision, real multi-step-execution tests (Package 5) prove the invalidation is actually consulted during real dispatch, not merely available as an unused capability.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (prop, integ) are supplied. Distinct row from 0064/0065 in the register's own denominator, but backed by the identical real mechanism - no duplicate derived-cache authority exists anywhere in execution.workflow (confirmed by test_workflow_authority.py, cited under 0328).
